questions.question: Which of the following statement is TRUE for Whole Numbers?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following statement is TRUE for Whole Numbers?

options.text: They include zero and positive integers.

questions.solution:
Whole numbers are defined as the set {0, 1, 2, 3, …} i.e. zero and all positive integers.

They do not include fractions, negatives, and do not start from 1 (they start from 0).

questions.question: Dhiraj goes to his school from his house at a speed of 3.8 km/hr and returns at 2.6 km/hr. If he takes 5 hours going and coming, the distance between his house and school is:
questions.questionHtml: Dhiraj goes to his school from his house at a speed of 3.8 km/hr and returns at 2.6 km/hr. If he takes 5 hours going and coming, the distance between his house and school is:
questions.solution:
Average speed for equal distances = 2ab/(a+b).

= 2 × 3.8 × 2.6 / (3.8 + 2.6)

= 19.76 / 6.4

= 3.0875 km/h.

Total distance in 5 h = 5 × 3.0875 ≈ 15.44 km.

One way distance = 15.44 / 2 ≈ 7.72 km.

questions.question: A rectangular aquarium (100 cm L × 50 cm W × 60 cm H) contains water with an initial level of 20 cm. 10 identical metal spheres, each with a diameter of 10 cm, are gently lowered into the aquarium. Assuming the spheres are fully submerged, what is the rise in the water level?
questions.questionHtml: A rectangular aquarium (100 cm L × 50 cm W × 60 cm H) contains water with an initial level of 20 cm. 10 identical metal spheres, each with a diameter of 10 cm, are gently lowered into the aquarium. Assuming the spheres are fully submerged, what is the rise in the water level?
questions.solution:
Volume of 10 spheres = 10 × (4/3)π(5)³ = (5000π/3) cm³.

Base area of aquarium = 100 × 50 = 5000 cm².

Rise = volume / base area = (5000π/3) / 5000 = π/3 cm.

questions.question: A floor is 12 m by 9 m. If tiles of 1.5 m × 1.5 m are used, how many tiles are needed?
questions.questionHtml: A floor is 12 m by 9 m. If tiles of 1.5 m × 1.5 m are used, how many tiles are needed?
questions.solution:
Area of floor = 12 × 9 = 108 m².

Area of 1 tile = 1.5 × 1.5 = 2.25 m².

Number of tiles = 108 / 2.25 = 48.

questions.question: A store sign is a 5 m × 4 m rectangle with a 2 m × 1 m rectangle cut out. Painting cost is ₹180/m². How much will the painting cost for the exposed area?
questions.questionHtml: A store sign is a 5 m × 4 m rectangle with a 2 m × 1 m rectangle cut out. Painting cost is ₹180/m². How much will the painting cost for the exposed area?
questions.solution:
Sign area = 5 × 4 = 20 m².

Cut-out area = 2 × 1 = 2 m².

Exposed area = 20 − 2 = 18 m².

Cost = 18 × 180 = ₹3,240.

questions.question: A regular hexagonal nut has outer side 6 cm and inner hollow side 3 cm. What is the material approximate area in the cross-section?
questions.questionHtml: A regular hexagonal nut has outer side 6 cm and inner hollow side 3 cm. What is the material approximate area in the cross-section?
questions.solution:
Area of regular hexagon = (3√3/2)s².

Outer area = (3√3/2)(36) = 54√3 ≈ 93.53 cm².

Inner area = (3√3/2)(9) = 13.5√3 ≈ 23.38 cm².

Material area = 93.53 − 23.38 ≈ 70.15 cm² ≈ 70 cm².

questions.question: A man got 10% of his investment as profit. If he invested Rs. 5000, and the profit was reinvested, what will be the total value after the second year with the same profit rate?
questions.questionHtml: A man got 10% of his investment as profit. If he invested Rs. 5000, and the profit was reinvested, what will be the total value after the second year with the same profit rate?
questions.solution:
This is compound growth at 10% for 2 years.

A = 5000 × (1.10)² = 5000 × 1.21 = ₹6,050.

questions.question: A triangular storage prism has a base shaped like a right triangle with side lengths in the ratio 5:12:13. If the total perimeter of the base is 60 cm and the height of the prism is 8 cm, calculate the lateral surface area of the prism.
questions.questionHtml: A triangular storage prism has a base shaped like a right triangle with side lengths in the ratio 5:12:13. If the total perimeter of the base is 60 cm and the height of the prism is 8 cm, calculate the lateral surface area of the prism.
questions.solution:
Sum of ratios = 30, so multiplier = 60/30 = 2.

Sides = 10, 24, 26 cm.

Lateral surface area = perimeter × height = 60 × 8 = 480 cm².

questions.question: If tanA = 3/4, then what is the value of sinA?
questions.questionHtml: If tanA = 3/4, then what is the value of sinA?
questions.solution:
tanA = 3/4 → opposite = 3, adjacent = 4, hypotenuse = √(3² + 4²) = 5.

sinA = opposite/hypotenuse = 3/5.

questions.question: If 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ, then what is the value of cosec²60° − cot²60°?
questions.questionHtml: If 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ, then what is the value of cosec²60° − cot²60°?
questions.solution:
Using the identity cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1 for every θ.

Hence cosec²60° − cot²60° = 1.

questions.question: If cos(90° − θ) = x and θ is acute, then what is the value of cos θ in terms of x?
questions.questionHtml: If cos(90° − θ) = x and θ is acute, then what is the value of cos θ in terms of x?
questions.solution:
cos(90° − θ) = sinθ = x.

For acute θ, cosθ = √(1 − sin²θ) = √(1 − x²).

questions.question: In a circle, a chord PQ subtends an angle of 50° at point R on the circumference. What is the angle it subtends at point S on the circumference, on the same side as R?
questions.questionHtml: In a circle, a chord PQ subtends an angle of 50° at point R on the circumference. What is the angle it subtends at point S on the circumference, on the same side as R?
questions.solution:
Angles in the same segment of a circle are equal.

Since R and S are on the same side of chord PQ, angle PSQ = angle PRQ = 50°.

questions.question: A circle with a radius of 20 cm. A chord of length 32 cm is drawn. What is the distance from the center of the circle to the chord?
questions.questionHtml: A circle with a radius of 20 cm. A chord of length 32 cm is drawn. What is the distance from the center of the circle to the chord?
questions.solution:
Half of chord = 16 cm.

Distance from centre = √(r² − (chord/2)²) = √(20² − 16²) = √(400 − 256) = √144 = 12 cm.

questions.question: In a circle, chord AB subtends an angle of 60° at the center. What is the angle subtended by the same chord AB at any point C on the major arc (opposite side of the center)?
questions.questionHtml: In a circle, chord AB subtends an angle of 60° at the center. What is the angle subtended by the same chord AB at any point C on the major arc (opposite side of the center)?
questions.solution:
Angle subtended at the centre = 2 × angle at the circumference (on the major arc).

60° = 2 × angle → angle = 30°.

questions.question: A line is drawn from a point P located 13 cm away from the center O of a circle with radius 5 cm. If the line is tangent to the circle, what is the length of the tangent from point P to the point of contact with the circle?
questions.questionHtml: A line is drawn from a point P located 13 cm away from the center O of a circle with radius 5 cm. If the line is tangent to the circle, what is the length of the tangent from point P to the point of contact with the circle?
questions.solution: Length of tangent = √(OP² − r²) = √(13² − 5²) = √(169 − 25) = √144 = 12 cm.
